about: Every module in packages/quac/src/parse/ and packages/quac/src/generate/ has a Python counterpart in quac_server/ of the same name, or is listed under modules with the reason it has none. A module with a counterpart exports each of its JavaScript functions under the Python name, or lists the function under functions with its reason. tests/test_parity.py checks both. Under departures, a function that does what its JavaScript counterpart does in a different way, and why.

modules.parse/parseBrandColour.ts: The project's Brand colour, which an application reads from the parsed project; no catalogue field carries it.
modules.parse/parseDataDefinedEditable.ts: A field's data-defined editable expression, for quac:editable_when, which is not in the first release.
modules.parse/parseExtent.ts: The map canvas extent, for quac:initial_view, which is not in the first release.
modules.parse/parseFormLayout.ts: The form layout, for quac:form_order, quac:in_form, quac:visible_when and quac:editable_when, which are not in the first release.
modules.parse/parseGetProjectSettings.ts: Reads a GetProjectSettings response, the other QGIS Server producer's input. The plugin reads the project's text.
modules.parse/parseMeasurement.ts: The project's area and distance units, for quac:measurement, which is not in the first release.
modules.parse/parseMergin.ts: The Mergin Maps plugin's filters, for quac:filters, which is not in the first release.
modules.parse/parseProjectVariables.ts: The project's variables, which an application reads from the parsed project; no catalogue field carries them.
modules.parse/parseRelations.ts: The project's relations, for quac:related_to, which is not in the first release.
modules.parse/parseStyle.ts: A layer's styles. The plugin's first release serves no style.
modules.parse/projectNotes.ts: The notes on what a project's catalogue does not carry, and the rules for Value Relations, relations and filters they share with the catalogue. Of a field's form settings the served catalogue carries only a Value Map's list and a Value Relation, and it carries no relations or filters, which are not in the first release. The rule finding a Value Relation's lookup is in generate/stac_catalogue.py.
modules.parse/qgisExpression.ts: Reads QGIS expressions, for defaults, constraints and conditional fields, which are not in the first release.
modules.parse/qtDateFormat.ts: Qt date patterns, for quac:date_format and for evaluating expressions, neither in the first release.
modules.parse/qtRegex.ts: Qt regular expressions, for evaluating expressions, which the first release does not do.
modules.parse/sqlFeatureFilter.ts: Evaluates a GDAL SQL feature filter against features, for an application that hands a layer's data to the public itself. QGIS Server applies a layer's filter when it serves the layer.
modules.generate/externalStacCatalogue.ts: Reads a STAC catalogue from somewhere else: another kind of source.
modules.generate/fileLayerCollection.ts: The Collection for a single data file: another kind of source.
modules.generate/folderStacCatalogue.ts: The folder of data files producer: another kind of source.
modules.generate/ogcFeaturesStacCatalogue.ts: The OGC API Features producer: another kind of source.
modules.generate/publishLayer.ts: Publishes a layer's features as QGIS Server would, for an application that hands a layer's data to the public itself. The plugin's catalogue points at QGIS Server, which publishes the features.
modules.generate/qmlForLayer.ts: Rebuilds a layer's QML style. The plugin's first release serves no style.
modules.generate/validateNewFeature.ts: Checks a new feature against a layer's field rules, for an application that adds features to a layer from a form it does not draw itself. The plugin's catalogue points at QGIS Server, which takes WFS transactions itself.

departures.generate/stacCatalogue.ts: generate_stac_catalogue writes each layer's data asset as buildAssets does for a file, WFS or ArcGIS layer, but writes no style asset, no via link to the project, no WMS, WMTS or XYZ link, and no quac:wfs_*, quac:arcgis_* or quac:max_zoom field. The style asset the JavaScript writes points into the project file (./<project>.qgs#<id>/<style>), and a catalogue written beside a QGIS project is to link QML files written beside it instead (vectoriahq/quac#69). An XYZ layer whose template uses {quadkey}, which the JavaScript writes as a data asset, gets none, since parse_data_source reads every source of the wms provider as kind image.
departures.parse/parseDataSource.ts: parse_data_source reads every source of the wms and xyzvectortiles providers as kind image, whatever its address; the JavaScript reads it as wms, wmts or xyz, or unsupported where the URL class refuses its address. In a served catalogue the kind decides only whether a layer is editable, and a layer of either provider is an image, which QGIS Server does not publish for WFS, so the server route makes it read-only either way. Vectoria chose this on 2026-11-07 over copying the URL class's rules into Python. An online file's address is written as the URL class writes its href by _url_href, which covers lower-casing the scheme and host, leaving off a default port, taking dot segments out of the path and percent-encoding what the class escapes; a host outside ASCII is converted with Python's IDNA 2003 codec, where the URL class uses UTS 46, so such a host can be written differently.
